prompt: A city library is opening a four-week evening pilot for adults who need help with online public services. It has one librarian, two volunteer tutors, eight computers, mostly drop-in visitors, and no budget for new software. Write a 450–600 word operating plan for the branch manager. Explain how to triage arrivals without needing to know why they came, give an example first evening, assign roles before and after the shift, and propose two concrete changes for week three depending on what the library observes. Include what tutors should do when someone needs help with a password or financial form.

Write a 450–600 word decision memo for a neighborhood food cooperative choosing between weekly home deliveries and two pickup hubs. The same van and volunteers serve both choices. The west neighborhood has frequent buses, the east neighborhood has unreliable buses, and some members cannot lift a full grocery box. Refrigerated items need to stay cold until handoff. Recommend a default service and exceptions, show how the recommendation follows from these constraints, and propose an affordable six-week pilot. Give the board a clear decision to make at the end of the pilot with concrete measurements, including who might be missing from the data.

A community garden wants to learn whether a new morning watering schedule reduces the number of plants that wilt by late afternoon. The garden has three beds. One is shaded after noon, another grows different varieties, and volunteers water whichever bed they arrive at first. Write a 450–600 word guide for volunteers on how to run a practical four-week comparison. Identify likely confounders, describe a matched assignment that volunteers can follow, specify exactly what to record on a wet or missed day, and describe how the coordinator should interpret a large average effect that appears in only one bed. Use everyday language.

Develop a 450–600 word teaching guide for the first session of a volunteer language class. Eight adult learners can understand more than they can say, one uses a hearing aid, and two have joined remotely through a single laptop. The goal is for every learner to ask for and clarify directions in a real conversation. Describe a ten-minute opening, two practice activities with sample dialogue, adaptations for mixed participation, and a short check for individual progress. Explain what the teacher should change by the second session if learners can read the example but struggle when a partner changes a detail.

Draft a 450–600 word briefing for a small museum after a sudden leak closed two galleries on a Saturday. The entrance remains open, reservations are sold out, and an accessible route to the third gallery is still available. The time to reopen is unknown. Write one short public update and an internal briefing for floor staff and the duty manager. Cover the first hour, visitor choices, how to handle conflicting information from contractors, and what facts would justify a revised public message. Use only the fictional facts given and identify any decisions that depend on new information.

Write a 450–600 word short story about two siblings who find conflicting recollections of the same ferry crossing while preparing a community oral history exhibit. Set the story during one evening in the room where they are arranging the display. Show how each sibling changes their mind through what they do with two objects already in the room, and use one brief conversation with a visitor to complicate the decision. End on a concrete choice for the exhibit that leaves room for both recollections. Write only the story.
